query: Trivy flags a HIGH CVE in msgpack in our production API image (python:3.12-slim, multi-stage, pip install --require-hashes from our lockfile). But msgpack is not in our lockfile or pyproject at all, and pip-audit over every manifest is clean. Is the Trivy finding a false positive I can dismiss?
expected_behavior: Explains where the package comes from: pip's own vendored tree (site-packages/pip/_vendor/) ships private copies of msgpack, urllib3, requests, certifi, etc. that no manifest pins and pip-audit never sees, while the image scanner correctly reports them
Says it is NOT a false positive and must not be dismissed as one

Prescribes the fix: do not ship the installer in the runtime image — uninstall pip (and setuptools/wheel) after the locked install in the final stage, or build the venv without pip and copy it in / use a distroless base
Notes that pinning msgpack in the app's own manifests cannot fix the alert (the vendored copy is a different file)
Gives a diff-checkable proof: `python -m pip --version` fails inside the image and/or the image SBOM lists no pip
anti_behavior: Dismisses the finding as a false positive or suppresses it in an ignore file
Adds msgpack to requirements/pyproject as the fix
Leaves pip in the runtime image
source: SKILL.md GitHub security alerts & Dependabot (scanner blind spot 4: an installer's vendored tree) + references/containers-and-orchestration.md (runtime stage ships no installer)
